title: Goods and Services of Marine Bivalves
abstract: This open access book addresses the ecological role of bivalves in the ecosystem that provides goods and services to society in a comprehensive way. These are defined as food for birds and benthos, habitat for species, regulation of water quality, sequestering carbon and nitrogen, and more.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Goods and Services of Marine Bivalves (2019), published by Springer Nature, has been cited 498 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 14,552 times.

Full narrative

Goods and Services of Marine Bivalves by Aad C. Smaal, Joao G. Ferreira, Jon Grant and others was published by Springer Nature in 2019. Conceptually, the work connects to Business, Fishery, Oceanography, Biology and Geology.

OpenAlex records 498 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2024 with 95 citing works. Notable citing venues include Aquaculture, The Science of The Total Environment and Frontiers in Marine Science. The citing works include 429 journal articles, 28 book chapters, 11 preprints and 9 reviews. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, the United Kingdom and China.

It has been downloaded 14,552 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 2 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Life below water among the Sustainable Development Goals.
